transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-23 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Evan Kline (CSM), Tom Ruiz (Solutions) - Summit: Alex Rivera (Security Lead), Maya Chen (Cloud Engineer), Samir Patel (Procurement), Leah Ortiz (Data Privacy)

Summary: walkthrough of customer SIG/CAIQ responses with emphasis on encryption, KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), evidence artifacts (SOC 2, pen test), and data residency requirements for EU customers. Discussed RBAC, SSO/SAML, audit logging retention, and private deployment options.

[00:00:12] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — Priya will run through the SIG items we've flagged as "needs evidence" and then we'll cover KMS options, residency and logging. i think alex you had a couple of priority items up front?

[00:00:28] Alex Rivera (Summit): yeah thanks. main, uh, priorities are — one, we need to confirm whether keys can be customer-managed and rotated on our schedule. two, audit logs retention and access, and three, how your VPC/private deployment affects data residency for our EU patients.

[00:00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): great, i'll start with the SIG mapping we did. just to set expectations, some fields on the CAIQ we answered as "provider asserts" and others are "see attached artifact". artifacts we usually provide: redacted SOC 2 Type II, pen test summary, ISO scoping statement where available, and architecture diagrams.

[00:01:12] Maya Chen (Summit): is the SOC 2 full report available? legal will want at least a redacted copy; they asked about third party subservice orgs.

[00:01:24] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II. redact customer-specific identifiers, we have an NDA-friendly version. we'll upload to the secure folder.

[00:01:38] Samir Patel (Procurement): also, for the SIG question about key management — can you confirm if Redwood supports bringing your own KMS keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS and the ability to rotate keys quarterly?

[00:01:55] Priya (Redwood SE): short answer: yes, for Redwood Private deployments we support customer-managed keys in the customer's cloud KMS. for our hosted offering we currently support a customer-managed KMS integration via a dedicated encryption envelope — but rotation policies differ, and there's an operational lead time. let me explain the flows.

[00:02:15] Priya (Redwood SE): flow A: Private/VPC deploy — keys live in customer's KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), we never persist plaintext and we use envelope encryption; you hold the root key. rotation is on your schedule and access is via KMS grants. Flow B: Hosted with CMK — you can provide a customer-managed key but we still maintain key grant lifecycle; quarterly rotation is possible but requires an ops change window. Flow C: Redwood-managed keys — simplest, but keys are rotated by Redwood per our policy.

[00:02:55] Leah Ortiz (Data Privacy): can you clarify "never persist plaintext" — does any metadata or derived artifacts contain PHI that could be reconstructed? our legal is strict about ePHI.

[00:03:10] Priya (Redwood SE): good question. the design is that we encrypt request payloads at rest with envelope encryption; KV cache entries and intermediate model state are encrypted. we avoid storing raw transcripts unless configured for retention; when retention is enabled, it's encrypted with the CMK. derived embeddings are treated as customer data and encrypted too. we do store limited metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts) for billing and routing — none of that should reconstruct ePHI. we'll mark that in the SIG notes.

[00:03:45] Alex Rivera (Summit): what about audit logs — who can see them and what retention? also, need exportable logs for our SIEM.

[00:03:58] Priya (Redwood SE): we provide audit logs at two layers: control plane (auth events, config changes, rollouts) and data plane (request start/stop, model served, token counts). For Private deployments logs can be sent to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/Stackdriver) or a syslog endpoint. Retention is configurable; default retention for control plane in hosted is 90 days, but enterprise add-on can extend. For Private, retention is in your environment so you control it.

[00:04:30] Jordan (Redwood AE): we also support export via S3 (encrypted) of logs and we've done customers that forward to Splunk/Sumo/Elastic — that's in the docs and we'll share the config snippet.

[00:04:45] Maya Chen (Summit): ok and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and want SCIM for user sync. are both supported?

[00:04:55] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC works with SAML attributes and you can map roles from IdP groups. for Private we can disable Redwood-managed accounts entirely. there are a few edge cases in older IdPs, but we've worked through them with customers.

[00:05:12] Alex Rivera (Summit): on compliance scope — do you have ISO 27001? some of our stakeholders expect ISO mention on the SIG.

[00:05:20] Jordan (Redwood AE): we maintain SOC 2 Type II. ISO 27001 is in progress for some regions; we can provide the current status and any certifications for specific subsystems. we'll call that out on the SIG as "in-scope" or "in-progress" as appropriate.

[00:05:36] Samir Patel (Procurement): another procurement question — indemnity and data residency clauses. our legal will want an EU data residency guarantee for EU customers; how does your private vs hosted offering affect that?

[00:05:49] Priya (Redwood SE): Private deployment in customer VPC or on-prem guarantees residency because data never leaves the customer's region. For hosted, we have region controls and can pin deployments to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 but we do not yet accept contractual data residency guarantees except as part of enterprise contracts. we'll flag that for legal.

[00:06:16] Leah Ortiz (Data Privacy): evidence — for the SIG question that asks for penetration test evidence, what do you provide? full report or summary?

[00:06:24] Jordan (Redwood AE): we provide an executive summary and remediation plan; full reports are usually redacted and only shared under an NDA. we can include the pen test scope and whether any critical/high findings were present and the mitigations.

[00:06:40] Priya (Redwood SE): on the CAIQ mapping, some of the "encryption in transit" questions we marked as "see TLS certs and cipher suites doc"; i'll attach the cipher suite list and TLS configuration. some customer forms ask for exact OpenSSL versions — sometimes transient, so we provide a snapshot and update cadence.

[00:07:02] Maya Chen (Summit): ok good. for the SIG item on "privileged access" can you detail who at Redwood has access to production keys and what break-glass looks like?

[00:07:14] Priya (Redwood SE): privileged access is role-based and audited. engineers do not have direct persistent access to customer CMKs; break-glass requires multi-party approval and is logged in the audit trail. for Private deployments, privileged access is yours unless you've contracted managed services. we'll create a short artifact describing the process.

[00:07:36] Alex Rivera (Summit): does Redwood have an HSM-backed option for the root key? our security team prefers HSM.

[00:07:44] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, if you use AWS CloudHSM or an HSM-backed KMS in your cloud, that's supported for Private. For hosted, we can integrate with HSM-backed CMKs in customer accounts on a case-by-case basis.

[00:07:58] Jordan (Redwood AE): competitor note — VendorX AI advertises BYOK for hosted; just to be clear, our hosted BYOK story has recently matured but for strict HSM guarantees customers prefer Private deployments.

[00:08:12] Samir Patel (Procurement): pricing impact? if we require Private + BYOK + extended log retention, is there a sizable premium?

[00:08:22] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes typically dedicated capacity + private networking + enterprise logging/retention is a higher tier. we'll include a preliminary pricing note in the follow-up.

[00:08:33] Priya (Redwood SE): quick demo time — i have a short slide that shows the envelope encryption diagram.

[00:08:40] [slide share audio faint] Priya (Redwood SE): top-level — client request encrypted with CMK->DEK envelope, decrypted in-memory in the worker with strict zeroing of mem after completion; KV cache entries encrypted with DEK; logs are separate and scrubbed of sensitive fields by default.

[00:09:05] Maya Chen (Summit): how do you scrub? there will be fields that might contain PHI in prompts.

[00:09:12] Priya (Redwood SE): we have redaction rules configurable by customer; default scrub will remove named entity patterns (SSNs, credit cards) but customers with strict needs should use their own pre-send redaction. we can also run a light NLP PII scrub, but note there are false positives/negatives.

[00:09:34] Alex Rivera (Summit): for the SIG evidence column that asks "who performs data classification" — we need a short statement. what's Redwood's position?

[00:09:44] Jordan (Redwood AE): we classify data as customer data, telemetry, and system data. customers are ultimately responsible for classification of their own content; we provide controls and default labels in the console. we'll add a sentence to the SIG that says so.

[00:09:58] [00:10:12] Priya (Redwood SE): lastly, on role mapping and SCIM — we can provide sample SAML attribute mapping and SCIM schema. If you give us a CSV of roles and required permissions we can propose a least-privilege mapping.

[00:10:30] Leah Ortiz (Data Privacy): retention windows for transcripts — can you set a 30-day default and auto-delete?

[00:10:38] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, retention is configurable per workspace. we have a retention API and we can set lifecycle rules. auto-delete is supported for Private and Hosted with enterprise controls.

[00:10:50] Jordan (Redwood AE): want to recap next steps and artifacts we'll send. Priya?

[00:10:55] Priya (Redwood SE): sure. we'll send: 1) redacted SOC 2 Type II and pen test executive summary; 2) KMS architecture diagram and short write-up describing BYOK vs Redwood-managed flows; 3) TLS/cipher suite snapshot; 4) SIG draft with our suggested responses flagged; 5) sample SAML/SCIM config snippets.

[00:11:20] Samir Patel (Procurement): and pricing note?

[00:11:24] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes we'll include a pricing appendix showing delta for Private + BYOK + 365-day log retention as an enterprise package.

[00:11:33] Alex Rivera (Summit): excellent. one more question — for the SIG there's a checkbox asking about "data residency guarantees" — can you provide a single-line answer we can paste?

[00:11:44] Jordan (Redwood AE): suggested line: "Redwood supports regionally isolated Private deployments that guarantee data residency within the customer's chosen cloud region; hosted region pinning is available via contract for enterprise customers." we'll put that exact phrasing in the draft.

[00:11:58] Maya Chen (Summit): ok great. that covers our key points. any risks we haven't called out?

[00:12:06] Priya (Redwood SE): the main operational risk is the rotation window for BYOK in hosted mode — it requires a planned change window. if you need immediate rotation testing we'd recommend a Private pilot. also, SCIM propagation delays can cause short-lived access sync issues — nothing critical but worth noting.

[00:12:27] Alex Rivera (Summit): thanks. can we get that follow-up by end of next week?

[00:12:33] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes, we'll aim for that. i'll send the folder link and upload artifacts.

[00:12:40] [cross talk / brief chatter about scheduling]

[00:12:55] Evan Kline (CSM): i'll book the follow-up deep-dive with our infra SEs for the week of July 6.

[00:13:05] Leah Ortiz (Data Privacy): thanks all. we'll review the SIG draft internally and get back with any edits.

[00:13:12] Jordan (Redwood AE): perfect. thanks everyone. end note: i'll capture the action items in the CRM and drop links in the shared thread.

[00:13:22] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-attribution and background noise noted; speaker labels approximate. some technical terms may be mangled (e.g., cloud region names).
